import numpy as np
# Note: In plotkit 'data_code' for curves, x and y1 are the current sheet's arrays.
# We modify them in place. The plotting library will apply these changes per file before combining.

# 1. Baseline subtraction using straight line between two points
# Point 1: Average of intensity at 1100 +/- 10 cm^-1
mask1 = (x >= 1090) & (x <= 1110)
if mask1.any():
    p1_x = np.mean(x[mask1])
    p1_y = np.mean(y1[mask1])
else:
    p1_x = 1100
    p1_y = np.interp(1100, x, y1)

# Point 2: Average of intensity at 1800 +/- 10 cm^-1
mask2 = (x >= 1790) & (x <= 1810)
if mask2.any():
    p2_x = np.mean(x[mask2])
    p2_y = np.mean(y1[mask2])
else:
    p2_x = 1800
    p2_y = np.interp(1800, x, y1)

# Linear baseline equation: y = mx + c
if p2_x != p1_x:
    slope = (p2_y - p1_y) / (p2_x - p1_x)
    intercept = p1_y - slope * p1_x
    baseline = slope * x + intercept
    y1 = y1 - baseline
else:
    y1 = y1 - p1_y

# 2. Normalize to G-band max (1550-1620 cm^-1)
g_mask = (x >= 1550) & (x <= 1620)
if g_mask.any():
    g_max = np.max(y1[g_mask])
    if g_max > 0:
        y1 = y1 / g_max
    else:
        y1 = y1 * 0 # Avoid div by zero
